accepted.s: A loan or advance is generally classified as a Non-Performing Asset when the interest or principal instalment remains overdue for more than:
accepted.x: An asset becomes an NPA when interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days.
accepted.tq: Use the precise numerical threshold rather than a nearby overdue period.
accepted.sec: NPA definition - overdue period, classification (standard, sub-standard, doubtful, loss)

accepted.s: In the case of farm loans, the overdue criterion for a short-duration crop is generally:
accepted.x: For short-duration crops, a farm loan is treated as overdue after two crop seasons.
accepted.tq: Distinguish crop-season rules from the general 90-day banking rule.
accepted.sec: NPA definition - overdue period, classification (standard, sub-standard, doubtful, loss)

accepted.s: For a farm loan relating to a long-duration crop, the overdue criterion is:
accepted.x: For long-duration crops, the relevant overdue period is one crop season.
accepted.tq: Test the confusable pair of one crop season and two crop seasons.
accepted.sec: NPA definition - overdue period, classification (standard, sub-standard, doubtful, loss)

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Standard asset — NPA for more than 12 months
Sub-standard asset — NPA for 12 months or less
Doubtful asset — regular account with no overdue
Loss asset — asset that has been fully recovered
accepted.x: A sub-standard asset is an NPA for 12 months or less. A doubtful asset is an NPA for more than 12 months, while a loss asset has been identified as a loss but may not yet have been written off.
accepted.tq: Match each classification with its exact time or recognition criterion.
accepted.sec: NPA definition - overdue period, classification (standard, sub-standard, doubtful, loss)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the new borrower-level NPA tagging system:
1. The system is to be effective from 1 April 2027.
2. If one loan of a borrower becomes an NPA, all loans of that borrower at the same bank become NPAs.
3. An account can be upgraded even if arrears on one facility remain unpaid.
4. Banks are required to identify NPAs through automated systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. An account is upgraded only after all arrears on every facility have been paid, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the single reversal in the condition for upgrading an account.
accepted.sec: NPA definition - overdue period, classification (standard, sub-standard, doubtful, loss)

accepted.s: Special Mention Accounts are best described as accounts which are:
o: Stressed but still classified as standard
Loans overdue for more than 180 days
accepted.x: Special Mention Accounts are stressed accounts that remain standard, generally involving overdue periods of 1 to 90 days.
accepted.tq: Separate an early-warning category from the NPA categories.
accepted.sec: Stress indicators - interest coverage ratio, SMA-0/1/2, restructured and stressed assets

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding Special Mention Accounts.
List-I
 a. SMA-0
 b. SMA-1
 c. SMA-2
 d. NPA
List-II
 i. 61–90 days overdue
 ii. More than 90 days overdue
 iii. 0–30 days overdue
 iv. 31–60 days overdue
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: SMA-0 covers 0–30 days, SMA-1 covers 31–60 days, SMA-2 covers 61–90 days, and an NPA is generally beyond 90 days overdue.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and eliminate codes with mismatched day bands.
accepted.sec: Stress indicators - interest coverage ratio, SMA-0/1/2, restructured and stressed assets

accepted.s: The usual progression of asset stress is:
o: NPA, SMA-2, SMA-1, SMA-0, standard asset
SMA-0, SMA-1, SMA-2, sub-standard, doubtful, loss
accepted.x: The sequence proceeds from SMA-0 to SMA-1 and SMA-2, followed by NPA classification as sub-standard, doubtful and loss.
accepted.tq: Arrange the stages from early stress to severe deterioration.
accepted.sec: Stress indicators - interest coverage ratio, SMA-0/1/2, restructured and stressed assets

accepted.s: Stressed assets comprise:
o: NPAs, restructured loans and written-off assets
Only gross NPAs and net NPAs
accepted.x: Stressed assets include NPAs, restructured loans and written-off assets.
accepted.tq: Test the exact components of a composite banking term.
accepted.sec: Stress indicators - interest coverage ratio, SMA-0/1/2, restructured and stressed assets

accepted.s: The Interest Coverage Ratio is calculated as:
o: Net profit divided by total assets
Interest due divided by operating earnings
Operating earnings divided by interest due
accepted.x: Interest Coverage Ratio equals operating earnings, or EBIT, divided by interest due.
accepted.tq: Recall the numerator-denominator order in the formula.
accepted.sec: Stress indicators - interest coverage ratio, SMA-0/1/2, restructured and stressed assets

accepted.s: If the Interest Coverage Ratio of a borrower is below 1, it indicates that:
o: The borrower has no outstanding debt
The borrower's earnings exceed its interest obligation
The borrower's earnings do not cover the interest due
The loan has necessarily been written off
accepted.x: An Interest Coverage Ratio below 1 means that operating earnings are insufficient to cover interest due.
accepted.tq: Apply the formula to interpret a risk indicator rather than merely recalling its definition.
accepted.sec: Stress indicators - interest coverage ratio, SMA-0/1/2, restructured and stressed assets

accepted.s: Net NPA is obtained by deducting which of the following from Gross NPA?
accepted.x: Net NPA is calculated as Gross NPA minus provisions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the stock of bad loans from the amount remaining after provisioning.
accepted.sec: Gross NPA vs net NPA - trend and peak year, PSB vs private banks

accepted.s: The GNPA ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks reached an approximate peak of 11.2 per cent in:
accepted.x: SCB GNPA peaked at approximately 11.2 per cent in March 2018, after the Asset Quality Review.
accepted.tq: Use the peak-year clue to distinguish pre-AQR, post-AQR and recovery-period figures.
accepted.sec: Gross NPA vs net NPA - trend and peak year, PSB vs private banks

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the SCB GNPA position in March 2025?
accepted.x: In March 2025, SCB GNPA was approximately 2.2–2.3 per cent and NNPA was 0.5 per cent.
accepted.tq: Match the date with the correct ratio instead of relying on the direction of the trend alone.
accepted.sec: Gross NPA vs net NPA - trend and peak year, PSB vs private banks

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about GNPA trends:
1. SCB GNPA was 4.28 per cent in March 2015.
2. SCB GNPA was approximately 11.2 per cent in March 2018.
3. SCB GNPA was 2.15 per cent in September 2025.
4. SCB GNPA was 1.93 per cent in March 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state the reported GNPA figures for the respective dates.
accepted.tq: Cross-check each date-value pair, especially the closely spaced 2025 and 2026 observations.
accepted.sec: Gross NPA vs net NPA - trend and peak year, PSB vs private banks

accepted.s: The GNPA of Scheduled Commercial Banks in March 2026, together with the corresponding NNPA, was:
accepted.x: In March 2026, GNPA was 1.93 per cent and NNPA was 0.39 per cent, described as a decadal low.
accepted.tq: Pair the two related ratios with the same reporting date.
accepted.sec: Gross NPA vs net NPA - trend and peak year, PSB vs private banks

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the banking-sector NPA trend?
1. GNPA has fallen for eight straight years.
2. Agriculture GNPA remains relatively high at about 6.0 per cent.
3. Agriculture GNPA is lower than 1 per cent.
4. September 2025 GNPA was reported at 2.15 per cent.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statement 3 is incorrect because agriculture GNPA was reported at about 6.0 per cent, with another estimate at 5.7 per cent. Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct.
accepted.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the reported sectoral trend.
accepted.sec: Gross NPA vs net NPA - trend and peak year, PSB vs private banks

accepted.s: Between March 2015 and March 2025, the GNPA ratio of Public Sector Banks declined from:
accepted.x: PSB GNPA declined from 4.97 per cent in March 2015 to 2.58 per cent in March 2025.
accepted.tq: Read both endpoints and check the direction of change.
accepted.sec: Gross NPA vs net NPA - trend and peak year, PSB vs private banks

accepted.s: Which of the following private-bank GNPA figures for June 2026 is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The reported June 2026 GNPA figures were HDFC 1.17 per cent, ICICI 1.38 per cent and Axis 1.28 per cent.
accepted.tq: Use institution-figure pairing to avoid swapping closely related percentages.
accepted.sec: Gross NPA vs net NPA - trend and peak year, PSB vs private banks

accepted.s: Provisioning Coverage Ratio is defined as:
o: Provisions held divided by total deposits
Gross NPAs divided by provisions held
Net NPAs divided by Gross NPAs
Provisions held divided by Gross NPAs
accepted.x: PCR is the ratio of provisions held to Gross NPAs.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the coverage ratio from its reciprocal.
accepted.sec: Provisioning coverage ratio and income recognition norms

accepted.s: The PCR of Scheduled Commercial Banks reported for March 2025 was:
accepted.x: The reported SCB PCR for March 2025 was 76.3 per cent. A higher figure of 93.14 per cent was also cited in a context that included technical write-offs.
accepted.tq: Match the exact percentage with the correct institutional aggregate and date.
accepted.sec: Provisioning coverage ratio and income recognition norms

accepted.s: Under income-recognition norms, interest on an NPA is booked as income:
o: Only when it is actually received
After the asset is written off
When it is accrued, whether or not received
accepted.x: Interest on an NPA is not recognised as income until it is actually received. This forms part of the IRACP framework.
accepted.tq: Apply the recognition rule to distinguish accrual from actual receipt.
accepted.sec: Provisioning coverage ratio and income recognition norms

accepted.s: IRACP stands for:
o: Indian Regulation of Accounts and Credit Policy
accepted.x: IRACP means Income Recognition, Asset Classification, Provisioning.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of a regulatory acronym.
accepted.sec: Provisioning coverage ratio and income recognition norms

accepted.s:
Match the stages of the Expected Credit Loss model with their provisioning treatment.
List-I
 a. Stage 1
 b. Stage 2
 c. Stage 3
 d. EIR method
List-II
 i. Lifetime expected loss
 ii. Effective interest rate method
 iii. 12-month expected loss
 iv. Full lifetime provision for credit-impaired assets
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Stage 1 involves 12-month expected loss, Stage 2 lifetime loss, Stage 3 full lifetime provision, and loss allowances use the effective interest rate method.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive EIR pair and then match the three stages by severity.
accepted.sec: Provisioning coverage ratio and income recognition norms

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Expected Credit Loss model:
1. Stage 1 applies to low-risk exposures.
2. Stage 2 applies when there is a significant rise in risk.
3. Stage 3 applies to credit-impaired assets, including those overdue for more than 90 days.
4. ECL may reduce Tier-1 ratios by 100–150 basis points.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct descriptions of the proposed three-stage ECL framework and its possible effect on Tier-1 ratios.
accepted.tq: Check whether the final quantitative implication is also supported rather than stopping at the conceptual statements.
accepted.sec: Provisioning coverage ratio and income recognition norms

accepted.s: The twin balance sheet problem refers to the simultaneous existence of:
o: High exports and low public debt
Fiscal surplus and excess bank liquidity
High household savings and low inflation
Over-leveraged corporates and capital-starved, NPA-laden banks
accepted.x: The twin balance sheet problem describes over-leveraged firms alongside capital-starved banks burdened with NPAs.
accepted.tq: Identify the two linked balance-sheet weaknesses rather than one symptom alone.
accepted.sec: Twin balance sheet problem - meaning, which Economic Survey framed it

accepted.s: The twin balance sheet problem was prominently framed in the Economic Survey:
accepted.x: The Economic Survey 2016–17, under Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian, discussed the festering twin balance sheet problem.
accepted.tq: Use the year and institutional context together to avoid nearby Economic Survey years.
accepted.sec: Twin balance sheet problem - meaning, which Economic Survey framed it

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the mechanism of the twin balance sheet problem:
1. Loan losses erode bank capital.
2. Banks may freeze new lending rather than recall old loans.
3. Private investment can decline as a result.
4. Over-leveraged firms are able to undertake fresh investment without difficulty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Over-leveraged firms face difficulty investing, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Trace the cause-effect chain and reject the statement that reverses its final effect.
accepted.sec: Twin balance sheet problem - meaning, which Economic Survey framed it

accepted.s: Aggressive lending during 2010–15 was especially associated with which sectors in the build-up of NPAs?
accepted.x: Aggressive lending to infrastructure, steel and power projects during 2010–15 contributed to the later NPA problem, particularly when projects stalled.
accepted.tq: Link the lending episode with the specific sectoral cluster.
accepted.sec: Causes of NPAs - infrastructure lending, evergreening, wilful defaulters

accepted.s: Which of the following external developments weakened borrowers' cash flows and contributed to NPAs?
o: A fall in domestic savings alone
The 2008 global financial crisis and weak exports
A sharp rise in agricultural exports alone
The introduction of GST and higher tax compliance
accepted.x: The 2008 crisis and weak exports adversely affected borrowers' cash flows and contributed to stress in bank assets.
accepted.tq: Select the paired external shocks that explain the deterioration in repayment capacity.
accepted.sec: Causes of NPAs - infrastructure lending, evergreening, wilful defaulters

accepted.s: A wilful defaulter is a borrower who:
o: Can pay but does not, or diverts borrowed funds
Cannot pay because of a temporary fall in income
Has an account overdue for less than 30 days
Has repaid the loan before its due date
accepted.x: A wilful defaulter has the capacity to repay but refuses to do so or diverts the borrowed funds.
accepted.tq: Distinguish deliberate non-payment from inability to repay.
accepted.sec: Causes of NPAs - infrastructure lending, evergreening, wilful defaulters

accepted.s: Evergreening of loans means:
o: Writing off all old loans immediately
Converting all NPAs into equity automatically
Giving fresh loans to repay old loans and conceal default
accepted.x: Evergreening involves extending fresh loans to repay old loans, thereby keeping the underlying default hidden.
accepted.tq: Recognise the concealment mechanism rather than confuse it with write-off or restructuring.
accepted.sec: Causes of NPAs - infrastructure lending, evergreening, wilful defaulters

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a direct effect of the Asset Quality Review on evergreening?
o: It strengthened the practice of concealing defaults
It reduced the need for provisioning
It ended the practice of evergreening by uncovering hidden stress
It converted all loans into standard assets
accepted.x: The Asset Quality Review exposed hidden stress and ended the practice of keeping defaults concealed through evergreening.
accepted.tq: Connect the regulatory intervention with its specific outcome.
accepted.sec: Causes of NPAs - infrastructure lending, evergreening, wilful defaulters

accepted.s:
Which combination correctly identifies two structural causes of NPAs?
1. Weak credit appraisal
2. Slow recovery laws
3. Automatic repayment by promoters
4. Strict appraisal of every infrastructure project
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Weak credit appraisal and slow recovery laws contributed to NPAs. Automatic repayment and strict appraisal are not causes identified in this context.
accepted.tq: Separate documented weaknesses from statements that describe their opposite.
accepted.sec: Causes of NPAs - infrastructure lending, evergreening, wilful defaulters

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages of the NPA vicious cycle in the correct sequence:
A. Provisioning and capital erosion
B. Aggressive lending and external shocks
C. Weak credit growth
D. Accumulation of NPAs
accepted.x: Aggressive lending and shocks lead to NPAs, which require provisioning and cause capital erosion, resulting in weak credit growth.
accepted.tq: Follow the causal sequence from initial shock to the final credit consequence.
accepted.sec: Causes of NPAs - infrastructure lending, evergreening, wilful defaulters

accepted.s: The Asset Quality Review was carried out by the RBI in:
accepted.x: The RBI conducted the Asset Quality Review in 2015.
accepted.tq: Recall the intervention year and distinguish it from the later NPA peak.
accepted.sec: Asset Quality Review - year, purpose, outcome

accepted.s: The principal purpose of the Asset Quality Review was to:
o: Increase bank deposits through higher interest rates
Uncover hidden NPAs and make banks recognise them
Provide automatic loan waivers to infrastructure companies
accepted.x: The AQR was designed to uncover hidden NPAs and ensure that banks recognised the underlying asset quality problems.
accepted.tq: Identify the regulatory purpose rather than a general banking reform objective.
accepted.sec: Asset Quality Review - year, purpose, outcome

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Asset Quality Review?
1. Disclosed NPAs increased sharply.
2. NPA levels peaked in 2018.
3. The twin balance sheet problem was exposed.
4. Hidden defaults continued to be classified as standard in all cases.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The AQR was intended to end, not perpetuate, the concealment of defaults as standard assets.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute reversal of the review's transparency objective.
accepted.sec: Asset Quality Review - year, purpose, outcome

accepted.s: The Government's 4R strategy in response to the banking-sector stress consisted of:
accepted.x: The four Rs were Recognise, Resolve, Recapitalise and Reform. The response included the IBC, recapitalisation and NARCL.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact expansion of a policy framework acronym.
accepted.sec: Asset Quality Review - year, purpose, outcome

accepted.s:
Which of the following measures formed part of the Government's response to the NPA problem under the 4R strategy?
1. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code
2. Bank recapitalisation
3. National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited
4. Abolition of provisioning norms
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The response included the IBC, recapitalisation and NARCL. Provisioning norms were not abolished.
accepted.tq: Identify the genuine policy instruments and eliminate the measure that contradicts banking prudence.
accepted.sec: Asset Quality Review - year, purpose, outcome
